title: Nondeterministic logarithmic-space decision
statement: Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, let $�	ext{Λ}$ be a finite set of machine states with decidable equality, and let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with $m$ registers, $d$ oracle languages $(A_j)_{j<d}$, and initial state $l_0$. Suppose every oracle language belongs to logarithmic space, and fix $K\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume that for every input $x$ there is a natural number $N$ such that every sequence of $N$ nondeterministic choices from the initial configuration (state $l_0$, all registers zero, and no answer recorded) halts; moreover, at every earlier prefix where the computation has not halted, its configuration satisfies the machine's precondition and, for every register $r$, the bit length of $r+1$ is at most $K(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$. Assume also that $x\in L$ if and only if some such sequence of $N$ choices leaves the answer true. Then $L$ belongs to nondeterministic logarithmic space.
